     Do not edit: the next build overwrites it. Change the manifest or the catalogue instead. -->

This page documents 23 commands, read off `cleon`'s command-line application as it is actually assembled - so it lists what can be typed, not what was intended.

Some commands are **environment-agnostic** and take no environment token; others are **environment-first** and take one between the product and the group (`cleon <env> <group> <command>`). Each command below says which it is, and its usage line shows the token where it belongs.

| Command | Environment | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cleon build` | agnostic | The whole build: fetch, compile, generate, package, install, zip. |
| `cleon build fetch-bundle` | agnostic | Pull the asbundle bundle for this host from the registry and unpack it. |
| `cleon build compile` | agnostic | Compile the model plugins, so the generator can load their Java functions. |
| `cleon build generate-sources` | agnostic | Run Actifsource headless: generate the plugin sources, features and update site, then validate. |
| `cleon build package` | agnostic | Compile, jar the plugins and features, and publish the P2 update site. |
| `cleon build install-features` | agnostic | Install the freshly built cleon features into the bundle's Eclipse. |
| `cleon build bundle` | agnostic | Zip the bundle, now carrying cleon, into a publishable archive. |
| `cleon release publish` | agnostic | Push the combined cleon+Actifsource bundle to the registry. |
| `cleon release publish-updatesite` | agnostic | Push the P2 update site to the registry (mechanics: the kernel's release:artifact). |
| `cleon deploy up` | env-first | Deploy the product to the target environment (placeholder). |
| `cleon deploy install` | env-first | Extract the packaged cleon bundle into a directory on this machine. |
| `cleon deploy down` | env-first | Tear the deployment down (placeholder). |
| `cleon deploy all` | env-first | Run build then deploy up end to end (the build->up dependency plan). |
| `cleon support install` | agnostic | Provision the host tooling the kernel needs - today oras; idempotent. |
| `cleon support site` | agnostic | Build the product's documentation website with Hugo, in Docker (HTML only). |
| `cleon support reference` | agnostic | Write the product's command reference as Markdown, read off its BUILT command line. |
| `cleon support git commit` | agnostic | git add -A + git commit -m. |
| `cleon support git push` | agnostic | git pull --rebase then push (current branch). |
| `cleon support git prune-branches` | agnostic | Delete local branches already merged into main (squash-aware via gh). |
| `cleon support git submodules` | agnostic | git submodule update --init lib/platform (init the submodule a fresh worktree needs). |
| `cleon support git auth-scopes` | agnostic | Grant the stored gh token the package scopes GHCR needs (interactive, idempotent). |
| `cleon support tasks catalogue` | agnostic | List the task coordinates the delivery kernel offers, marking the namespaces this product's commands reach. |
| `cleon support tasks generate` | agnostic | Regenerate the product's CLI module from its manifest (--check reports drift and writes nothing). |

## build

### `cleon build`

```text

```

The group's default action: `cleon build` with no subcommand runs this.

The whole build: fetch, compile, generate, package, install, zip.

## support git

Environment-agnostic: these commands take no environment token - `cleon support git <command>`.

### `cleon support git commit`

```text
cleon support git commit [MESSAGE...]
```

Also spelled `cleon commit`.

git add -A + git commit -m.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MESSAGE...` | text | none | commit message |

### `cleon support git push`

```text
cleon support git push
```

Also spelled `cleon push`.

git pull --rebase then push (current branch).

### `cleon support git prune-branches`

```text
cleon support git prune-branches [--dry-run] [--remote] [--unmerged]
```

Also spelled `cleon prune-branches`.

Delete local branches already merged into main (squash-aware via gh).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run`, `-n` | flag | `False` | preview only |
| `--remote` | flag | `False` | also delete merged branches on origin |
| `--unmerged` | flag | `False` | ALSO delete branches that cannot be proven merged (destructive) |

### `cleon support git submodules`

```text
cleon support git submodules
```

Also spelled `cleon submodules`.

git submodule update --init lib/platform (init the submodule a fresh worktree needs).

### `cleon support git auth-scopes`

```text
cleon support git auth-scopes
```

Also spelled `cleon auth-scopes`.

Grant the stored gh token the package scopes GHCR needs (interactive, idempotent).

## Platform tasks this product has not placed

These are coordinates the delivery kernel's catalogue offers that no command of this product instantiates, so they are in no group above and cannot be typed here. The list is what the PLATFORM offers - not what this manifest imports, which for a flat-form manifest is a separate declaration.

Adopting one is not always just a command declaration. Some of them read product data of their own - a manifest section, a configuration file, a running environment - and placed without it they would fail on their first line; others need nothing but the declaration. The kernel's catalogue says, at each coordinate, which of the two it is.

| Task | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `docs:render` | Render the project docs via docToolchain (generateHTML + generatePDF) in Docker. |
| `release:artifact` | Publish a declared directory to a registry as an OCI artifact. |
| `support:claude-plugins` | Install the Claude Code plugins declared in the manifest's `claude` section; idempotent. |
| `support:environments` | List the named environments and the backend each targets, marking the active one. |
| `support:nexus` | Drive the LAN Sonatype Nexus artefact proxy: up \| down \| status \| repos \| cleanup. |
| `test:accept` | Run the lab-based suites in sequence against the running lab. |
| `test:gate` | Run a declared pytest suite against the running lab. |
| `test:report` | Merge the unit results into the shared Allure results and render the HTML archive. |
| `test:typecheck-python` | Type-check the product's Python sources with mypy, in the host venv (no Docker, no lab). |
